يترازانان: يَتَرَازَانَانِ 6 , said of two mountains, They are opposite, or facing, each other. (K.)
يتعاقبان: يَتَعَاقَبَانِ 6 (T, S, O, Msb, TA) They follow each other [by turns]; or alternate; (T, Msb, TA;) one coming and the other going; (TA;) said of the night and the day; (T, Msb;) or as the night and the day; (S, O, TA;) as also 🡻يَعْتَقِبَانِ. (TA.) You say, تَعَاقَبَ المُسَافِرَانِ عَلَى الدَّابَّةِ The two travellers rode upon the beast, each of them in his turn. (TA: and the like is said in the Msb.) And تعاقبا عَمَلًا They two did a work, or deed, by turns, or alternately: syn. اِرْتَوَحَاهُ, (K and TA in art. روح,) and تَرَاوَحَاهُ (TA in that art.) And تعاقبا They helped each other by turns. (TA.) And 🡻يَعْتَقبَانِهِبِالضَّرْبِ They two ply him by turns with beating (A.) See also 3, near the beginning. التَّعَاقُبُ also signifies The coming to water [by turns, or] time after time. (TA.)
يتلاويان: يَتَلاَوَيَانِ 6 said of two serpents [They twist together]: see عَقاَمٌ, last sentence.
